findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted: slug is set only when billing is enabled
findings.body: The first hunk replaces `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` with `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which drops the negation. When billing is disabled, the organization is now created without a `slug`. When billing is enabled, `slug` is written immediately, bypassing the `requestedSlug` metadata on line 153 that the billing flow relies on for pending slugs. Restore the original guard: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. The second hunk (line 153) is a pure rewrite with the same meaning and is fine.

findings.title: Meet fallback dereferences a possibly empty destination list
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` has no optional chaining. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and that value reaches `EventManager.create`. For a Google Meet event type in that state, this line throws a TypeError. Base read `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`. Confidence is medium because it depends on an organizer without a destination calendar, which I could not check at runtime.

findings.title: updateLocation writes calendar references without credential or calendar id
findings.body: `updateEvent` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-322) returns neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`, so `result.externalId` (line 208) and `result.credentialId ?? undefined` (line 209) are always undefined. Base used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `destinationCalendar?.credentialId` here. `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/editLocation.handler.ts:119-121` appends these rows to the booking's references, so the calendar reference now has no calendar id. Later cancel and reschedule then call deleteEvent/updateEvent with a null externalCalendarId. Google then falls back to 'primary' (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317), or the cancel takes the legacy all-credentials path (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:473-481). Fix: have updateEvent return the credential id and externalId, or fill them from the booking reference or destination here.

findings.title: Legacy destinations without credentialId lose their calendar id
findings.body: `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:159). For a destination with no credentialId, this branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the destination's externalId. The result's externalId is therefore undefined, and the reference is stored with no externalCalendarId (line 169). Base stored `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` there. Google's createEvent also cannot match a destination by credentialId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-149), so it inserts into 'primary' instead of the user's chosen calendar. Pass `destination.externalId` through this branch, and have Google fall back to the destination without a credentialId.

findings.title: Per-destination externalId is recorded but never used by Office365, Lark or CalDAV
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents passes `destination.externalId` into `createEvent` (line 370), and packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:235-236 drops it: `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. Office365 (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-77), Lark (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129) and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-164) all still read `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event with a second member on one of these apps, the call goes to the first member's calendar id with the second member's token. CalDAV filters to no calendars and creates nothing. CalendarManager.ts:267-268 still reports that destination's externalId and credential id, so the booking reference points at a calendar where no event exists. Google avoids this by matching on credentialId (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-149). Either pass externalId into the calendar services and use it in each, or select by credentialId as Google does.

findings.title: Google delete falls back to 'primary' when no externalCalendarId is passed
findings.body: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` with a null or undefined externalCalendarId never matches a stored externalId, so `calendarId` is always undefined here and the delete goes to 'primary' (line 322). Base used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The null case happens: EventManager.ts:505-509 passes null when the reference has no externalCalendarId, and the finding on EventManager.ts:208 creates such references. A 404 is resolved silently (line 335), so the event stays on the user's selected calendar and the cancellation reports success. Use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, or the credential-matched destination, when externalCalendarId is empty. The same lookup is in updateEvent at line 256.

findings.title: Google update sends an undefined calendarId when no externalCalendarId is passed
findings.body: Same lookup as line 317. With an empty externalCalendarId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined and `calendar.events.update` (line 261) is called without a calendarId. I did not verify how googleapis handles a missing path parameter, but the request cannot target the existing event. CalendarManager.ts:295-304 swallows the error and returns success false. Base used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

findings.title: Google create: patch uses undefined calendarId while insert falls back to 'primary'
findings.body: The insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (line 154), but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the Meet link (line 168) uses the raw `selectedCalendar`, which is undefined when no destination matches credentialId. The patch is silently not applied, so the event in 'primary' has no hangout link in its description. Use the same resolved id for insert and patch. The legacy destination case is covered by the EventManager.ts:380 finding.

findings.title: Collective team destinations are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` (line 1078) then does nothing, and the members' calendars are never used. Base also used only the organizer's calendar, so this is not a regression, only an incomplete path. Build the array when it is null, or state in the PR that this case is intentionally unsupported.

findings.title: Webhook payloads now carry destinationCalendar as an array
findings.body: `webhookData` spreads `...evt` (lines 1754-1755), so BOOKING_* webhook payloads now send `destinationCalendar` as an array (or []) where they previously sent an object or null. The e2e fixture was changed to `[]` (apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249), which confirms the new shape. Integrators that read `destinationCalendar.externalId` will break, and the PR body does not mention it. Confirm this is intended, and either keep the singular field in the payload or document the change.

findings.title: Legacy cancel branch runs once per calendar reference
findings.body: The `else` branch (lines 473-481) loops every calendar credential and sits inside the per-reference loop that starts at line 423. A booking with several reference rows that lack credentialId deletes the same uid on each matching credential once per row. The recurring branch (lines 444-461) has the same shape. Hoist the legacy branch out of the loop, or run it once when no reference has a credentialId.

findings.title: loadUsers error mapping changed
findings.body: An empty `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain Error (line 728), which the catch at lines 757-761 turns into a 500 'Unable to load users' instead of a 4xx. Prisma errors are returned as HTTP 400 with the raw Prisma message (lines 758-759). Base returned the empty list and let later checks decide. Map the validation error to a 400 with its message, and keep raw Prisma messages out of client-facing errors.

findings.title: New multi-destination create and update paths have no tests in this part
findings.body: The PR changes createAllCalendarEvents, updateAllCalendarEvents, and the Google, Office365 and Lark services, but no file in this part adds or changes a unit test; the only test file touched is apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts. The defects above would be caught by a test that creates events for two destinations, then updates or cancels with a null externalCalendarId. Confidence is medium because test files outside this part may exist.
